items.followUp: Write the steps to create and view a webpage in HTML.

rubric.why: Shows the basic process of writing and saving an HTML file.
rubric.description: Write HTML code in a text editor and save the file with an .html extension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing HTML code and saving it as an HTML file.

rubric.why: Shows how to view the created webpage.
rubric.description: Open the saved HTML file in a web browser.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for opening or viewing the file in a browser.

modelAnswer: Open a text editor and write the webpage using HTML tags.
Save the file with an .html extension, then open it in a web browser.

rubric.why: Identifies the base of the hexadecimal system.
rubric.description: State that hexadecimal is a base-16 number system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its base as 16.

rubric.why: Identifies the symbols used to write hexadecimal numbers.
rubric.description: State that it uses the digits 0–9 and the letters A–F.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the symbols.

modelAnswer: The hexadecimal number system is a base-16 number system.
It uses the symbols 0–9 and A–F.

items.followUp: How is text represented in computer memory?

rubric.why: Identifies the binary form used for storing data.
rubric.description: State that data is represented in binary form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning binary or bits.

rubric.why: Identifies the two values represented in memory.
rubric.description: Explain that memory represents data using 0s and 1s.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the two values.

modelAnswer: A computer represents data in memory in binary form.
The data is stored as bits, each having a value of 0 or 1.

items.followUp: Construct the truth table for the OR operator.

rubric.why: Checks the AND output for input combinations other than 1,1.
rubric.description: Show an output of 0 for inputs 0,0; 0,1; and 1,0.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly showing the three rows with output 0.

rubric.why: Checks the AND output when both inputs are 1.
rubric.description: Show an output of 1 for inputs 1,1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly showing the 1,1 row with output 1.

items.followUp: Briefly describe patent protection for an invention.

rubric.description: State that copyright law provides legal protection for original work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning legal protection.

rubric.why: Identifies whose work or rights are protected.
rubric.description: Explain that it protects the rights of the creator or owner to use and distribute the work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the creator's or owner's rights.

modelAnswer: Copyright law gives legal protection to original works such as books, music, software, and other creative work.
It protects the creator's rights to use, copy, and distribute the work.

items.followUp: How does a domain name relate to an IP address?

rubric.why: Uses the telephone-address comparison asked for in the question.
rubric.description: Relate a telephone number to an address that identifies a particular telephone.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a telephone number identifies a phone.

rubric.why: Connects the analogy to network addressing.
rubric.description: Explain that an IP address identifies a computer or device on a network, like a telephone number identifies a phone.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly relating an IP address to a network device.

modelAnswer: A telephone number identifies a particular telephone.
Similarly, an IP address identifies a computer or device on a network.

items.followUp: What is the Internet? Give one example of a service it provides.

rubric.why: Identifies the example of a network of networks.
rubric.description: Name the Internet as a network of networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the Internet.

rubric.why: Shows why the Internet is an example.
rubric.description: State that the Internet connects many networks together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as interconnected networks.

modelAnswer: The Internet is an example of a network of networks.
It connects many computer networks around the world.

items.followUp: For which words does URL stand?

rubric.why: Checks the first word of the expansion.
Checks the remaining words of the expansion.
rubric.description: Expand the remaining letters as Transfer Protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating “Transfer Protocol”.

modelAnswer: HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
